Chapter Four: Overcoming Barriers to Finding the Element.
Let’s be honest—the road to discovering your Element is rarely a smooth one. Along the way, you’re bound to run into obstacles. Some you can see coming, while others sneak up from inside. Think about it: cultural expectations, family pressures, even your own self-doubt... these can all make it tough to pursue what truly lights you up.
Imagine a young man growing up in a family of doctors. From the very start, he felt the weight of expectation. Medicine was seen as the one respectable path, and anything outside of science? Well, that was brushed off as a waste of time. But here’s the twist—he secretly loved photography. He’d spend hours capturing moments, framing the world through his lens. Yet, he kept it hidden, scared of letting down the people who mattered most.
This kind of pressure isn’t rare. Most of us are taught to value security over satisfaction, to play it safe instead of chasing what’s meaningful. The fear of failure, or the worry about disappointing others, can be downright paralyzing. Before you know it, you start to believe that dreams are for someone else—someone without the responsibilities you carry.
But barriers aren’t always loud and obvious. Sometimes, they’re quiet. There was a woman, for example, who seemed to have it all—a successful career, respect, the works. Yet deep down, something felt off. She couldn’t figure out why. It wasn’t until she started volunteering at a local theater that things clicked. The thrill of being on stage brought back a joy she hadn’t felt in years.
So, how do you push past these barriers? It takes courage. You’ve got to be willing to question what you’ve always assumed, to try something new, and yes, to risk feeling vulnerable. But you don’t have to go it alone. Having support—whether it’s from a mentor, a friend, or even a stranger—can make a huge difference.
Picture a student struggling to find her way. A mentor, who listened without judgment and offered gentle advice, opened her eyes to possibilities she’d never considered. With that encouragement, she started exploring her passion for design, eventually building a career that blended art with technology. Sometimes, all it takes is one person believing in you.
And support can show up in unexpected ways. Maybe it’s a random conversation, or just a passing comment that sparks a new direction. The important thing is to stay open—to new ideas, to feedback, and to the belief that it’s never too late to make a change.
Here’s something you should remember: your age, your background, your circumstances—they don’t have to be barriers. People have found new passions in their seventies, switched careers after decades, or stumbled into fulfillment in the most surprising places. What they all share is that willingness to listen to that quiet voice inside that whispers, “There’s more out there for me.”
When people operate from their Element, everyone benefits. They bring energy, creativity, and a sense of purpose to whatever they do. But let’s be real—the path to fulfillment isn’t a straight line. The clues to what truly moves us are often tucked away in the things we do when no one else is watching.
This journey? It’s always ongoing. There’ll be doubts, setbacks, and opinions flying at you from every direction. But every step you take toward your Element is a step toward a life that feels real, and meaningful. The world needs people who are alive to their own potential—people willing to take risks and follow their curiosity.
